title: Every Reactor Package ships its own subgraph and Switchboard composes them into one endpoint
content:
## No monolithic schema

Switchboard does not expose one hand-maintained schema. Every Reactor Package ships its **own** GraphQL schema fragment — its subgraph — and Switchboard composes all of them into a single unified endpoint at `/graphql`.

The practical payoff is cross-package querying. A client can pull data owned by two completely independent packages in one request, and neither package needs to know the other exists:

```graphql
query {
  todoList(id: "doc-123") {
    id
    todos {
      id
      title
      done
    }
  }
}
```

That query hits one endpoint. Behind it, whichever package owns the `todoList` type resolves it.

## Each subgraph exposes three things

- **Queries** — for reading documents and processor read models.
- **Mutations** — for dispatching actions to documents.
- **Custom types** — the domain-specific GraphQL types your resolvers return.

## Why this makes the package the unit of delivery

Because a package owns its subgraph, shipping the package ships its API. There is no central schema registry to update, no coordination step, no separate gateway config to edit. Installing a package into a Switchboard extends the supergraph.

Composition is also not a one-shot boot step. `GraphQLManager` keeps subgraphs in a map keyed by supergraph name, registers each one, and rebuilds the router; document-model subgraphs are *regenerated* when models are loaded dynamically, so packages installed after startup still land in the composed schema. Duplicate subgraph names are skipped rather than merged — a name collision silently loses the second registration.

One endpoint is not quite everything: the per-drive subgraph is served separately at `/d/:driveId` and is deliberately excluded from the `/graphql` supergraph.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/02-Learn/06-switchboard/02-subgraphs.mdx, packages/reactor-api/src/graphql/graphql-manager.ts (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: Package-owned schema fragments are stitched into a supergraph, so one query can span independent packages. Shipping a package ships its API — there is no central schema registry.
